text: <highlight>Stored XSS</highlight> is the most dangerous type of XSS. The malicious script is permanently stored on the target server (e.g., in a database). When a victim navigates to the affected page, the browser retrieves the script and executes it automatically.

title: Execution Stages
items: **Injection:** The attacker finds an input field (comments, profile bio, message board) that saves to a database.
**Storage:** The server fails to sanitize the input and saves the raw JavaScript string.
**Execution:** Every user who loads that page pulls the script from the database and runs it in their own browser context.
**Impact:** Can be used for mass cookie theft, redirecting all visitors to a phishing site, or defacing the website.

text: Why it is NOT Reflected XSS

Unlike Reflected XSS, which requires a victim to click a <highlight>malicious link</highlight>, Stored XSS is passive. The victim only needs to browse the legitimate website normally to be compromised. It is 'Stored' because the payload lives in the web application's data.

title: How to Stop Persistent Scripts
items: **Input Validation:** Only allow expected characters (e.g., alphanumeric only for usernames).
**Output Encoding:** Convert characters like < to < so the browser treats them as text, not code.
**Content Security Policy (CSP):** Restrict which scripts can run and where they can load from.
